claim: Pattern recognition becomes routine in medical imaging
originalWording: Pattern recognition becomes routine in medical imaging

sources.title: Spiritual Machines: The Merging of Man and Machine — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: P02 Health care in 2009, pattern-recognition bullet

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Computer pattern recognition is used routinely in important diagnostic imaging workflows.
reference.rationale: Computer-aided detection accompanied 74% of Medicare screening mammograms in 2008, a concrete routine clinical workflow. This fulfills routine use even though CAD does not always improve outcomes. It does not require autonomous diagnosis in every specialty.

evidence.title: Rao et al.: Trends in utilization of CAD mammography, 2004–2008
evidence.note: Computer-aided detection accompanied 74% of Medicare screening mammograms in 2008. Routine use is established, not improved accuracy or autonomous diagnosis..
